fields.System.Title: INT-1 — Inbound integration
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Take messages from the ERP and turn them into WMS records — rejecting the bad ones loudly and
never creating the same thing twice.

Scope

In. ASN, order, and master data intake; malformed message handling; deduplication.

Out. The ERP itself. Message transport choice.

Design notes

Validate at the edge, hard. A bad message accepted becomes bad master data, and bad master
data becomes wrong stock — slowly, across every transaction that touches it. Reject immediately
with a reason naming the offending field.

Never let an inbound message change stock directly. The ERP can tell you what it expects.
It cannot tell you what is on the shelf. Stock changes only through warehouse actions.

INT-104 prevents the worst integration failure: a malformed message silently dropped, so
the ERP believes in an order the WMS has never heard of. Failed messages go to a dead-letter
table with the error and the original payload, and someone reviews it daily.

INT-105 is cheap and prevents double shipments. Unique constraint on
(source_system, external_reference). Treat a repeat as already processed and return the
original result.

Master data updates need per-field thinking. Some changes are safe to apply
automatically — a description. Some must be rejected while stock exists — case quantity,
tracking flags. See [FDN-607](../../stories/FDN/FDN-607-freeze-fields.md).

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| ERP retry creating a duplicate order | [doc 09 §3.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Malformed message dropped silently | [doc 08 §6](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Frozen master data field changed by an ERP update | [doc 03 §5](../../../docs/03-master-data.md) |
| Bad data accepted at the edge | [doc 03 §7](../../../docs/03-master-data.md) |
